drug_class: Neurotoxin / Muscle relaxant (botulinum toxin type A)
purpose: OnabotulinumtoxinA is used to treat a variety of conditions including chronic migraines, muscle spasms, overactive bladder, excessive sweating, and certain eye muscle problems. It is also used cosmetically to smooth facial wrinkles and fine lines. Your doctor may prescribe it for other conditions where relaxing certain muscles or glands is helpful.
how_it_works: This medication works by temporarily blocking the signals your nerves send to your muscles or glands, causing them to relax or stop overworking. Think of it like pressing a pause button on the muscle or gland that is causing problems. The effects are not permanent, so the treatment usually needs to be repeated every few months.
common_side_effects: Headache, pain, swelling, or bruising at the injection site, flu-like symptoms, drooping eyelids or eyebrows (temporary), dry eyes, and neck pain or muscle weakness near where the injection was given.
warnings: In rare but serious cases, the toxin can spread beyond the injection site and cause difficulty swallowing, speaking, or breathing — call 911 or get emergency help right away if this happens. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, especially antibiotics or blood thinners, as they can interact with this drug. Do not use if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first. Never get injections from unlicensed providers, as improper use can be very dangerous.
typical_dosing: The dose and how often you receive injections depends on what condition is being treated. For example, chronic migraines are typically treated every 12 weeks with multiple small injections around the head and neck. For cosmetic wrinkles, small amounts are injected into specific facial muscles every 3 to 6 months. Your doctor will determine the right dose and schedule for your specific needs.
